the tanna R' Yonatan, R' Yishmael's student, narrator of the baraita at 70b.12-71a.1 (not the amora)
in the Nidda mishna cited at 71a.9-12
the Sages of the Nidda mishna (71a.13)
anonymous redactorial voice of this sugya

props.gloss_en: a fetus that died inside a kosher animal, touched by the shepherd's hand -- [the shepherd is] pure
the first tanna: inside a non-kosher animal too -- pure
R' Yosei HaGelili: inside a non-kosher animal -- impure
Rav Chisda: the first tanna's reason is a kal vachomer -- if its mother avails to permit it for eating, she avails to purify it from nevela-impurity
'and when [one] of the animals dies' (Lev 11:39) -- this is a non-kosher animal
'of those that are yours to eat' -- this is a kosher animal
R' Yitzchak: R' Yosei HaGelili's source is Lev 11:27 -- paw-walkers inside a living animal I made impure for you
'among any chaya' means paw-walkers inside a [living] chaya
the verse means paw-walkers inside four-walkers; a klut in a cow is a four-walker inside an eight-walker
Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak: rather from Lev 5:2 -- does only a non-kosher carcass defile and a kosher one not? rather this is the fetus, impure inside a non-kosher animal and pure inside a kosher one
Lev 5:2 states 'or the carcass of a non-kosher behema' alongside 'the carcass of a non-kosher chaya'
without R' Yitzchak's verse one would say Lev 5:2 comes wholly for Rebbi's teaching; it teaches that the verse also yields the fetus law
R' Yonatan: we learned that the carcass of a kosher behema defiles
...and that the carcass of a non-kosher behema defiles
...and that the carcass of a non-kosher chaya defiles
R' Yonatan: we did not learn the carcass of a kosher chaya -- from where?
ben Azzai: [the kosher chaya's carcass defiles] from Lev 11:27, 'among any chaya'
R' Yonatan: does it say 'and any chaya'? it says only 'among any chaya' -- it comes for paw-walkers inside a chaya
ben Azzai: and what does Yishmael say in this matter?
R' Yishmael: a chaya is included in [the term] behema
R' Yishmael: and a behema is included in [the term] chaya
R' Yishmael: a kosher chaya is included in kosher behema
R' Yishmael: a non-kosher chaya is included in non-kosher behema
R' Yishmael: a non-kosher behema is included in non-kosher chaya
R' Yishmael: a kosher behema is included in kosher chaya
ben Azzai, in these words: woe to ben Azzai, who did not serve R' Yishmael
the stam: chaya is included in behema -- Deut 14:4-5 lists deer and gazelle under 'these are the behema you may eat'
the stam: behema is included in chaya -- Lev 11:2-3, 'these are the chaya you may eat among all the behema'
kosher chaya under kosher behema -- for the signs [of kosher species]
non-kosher chaya under non-kosher behema -- for [the prohibition of] cross-mating
non-kosher behema under non-kosher chaya -- for Rebbi's teaching
Rebbi: Lev 5:2's liability concerns impurity [in relation to] sacred things, as at Lev 7:21
kosher behema under kosher chaya -- for 'formation' [of offspring], as the Nidda mishna (R' Meir) has it
R' Meir: a woman who miscarries the form of a behema, chaya or bird, kosher or not, observes the periods of a birth (male, female, or both if unknown)
the Sages: whatever is not of human form is not [counted] a child

הולך -- וכל הולך: the extra 'all' includes a cow-fetus inside a camel

supports.gloss_en: לכדרבי, דתניא: רבי אומר אקרא אני חיה, בהמה למה נאמרה -- the baraita in which Rebbi uses the 'behema' clause
ליצירה, דתנן: המפלת מין בהמה חיה ועוף... תשב לזכר (marker דתנן, a mishna; no distinct kind exists)

objections.gloss_en: אלא מעתה, קלוט במעי פרה ליטמא, דמהלכי כפים בחיה הוא? -- then a solid-hoofed fetus inside a cow should be impure

answered_by.gloss_en: מהלכי כפים במהלכי ארבע, והאי מהלכי ארבע במהלכי שמנה הוא (= p_arba_bimhalchei_arba)

objections.gloss_en: פרה במעי גמל לא תטמא, דמהלכי שמנה במהלכי ארבע הוא -- then a cow-fetus inside a camel should not be impure

answered_by.gloss_en: הולך, וכל הולך -- לרבות פרה במעי גמל (the ribui ribui_vechol_holech)

objections.gloss_en: קלוט במעי קלוטה ליטמא, דמהלכי ארבע במהלכי ארבע הוא! -- then a solid-hoofed fetus inside a solid-hoofed [kosher] cow should be impure

answered_by.gloss_en: להכי אהני קל וחומר דרב חסדא -- that is what Rav Chisda's kal vachomer (kv_imo_matirto) is for: every kosher animal's fetus is pure

objections.gloss_en: מתקיף לה רב אחדבוי בר אמי: חזיר במעי חזירתא לא ליטמא, דמהלכי שמנה במהלכי שמנה הוא! -- unanswered; אלא follows at 70b.9
וכי נאמר וכל חיה? והלא לא נאמר אלא בכל החיה -- the verse is spent on paw-walkers inside a chaya, not on the kosher chaya's carcass
